subject: maths
promptStrong: Give me a 6-mark exam-style question on {lo} for {board} {level} {subject}, then mark my answer against the mark scheme.
promptWeak: Explain {lo} for {board} {level} {subject} simply, with a worked example and the most common mistake students make.

questions.q: A circle has radius 4 cm. What is its area? (Use π ≈ 3.14)
Two angles lie on a straight line. One is 110°. What is the other?
questions.explain: Angles on a straight line sum to 180°, so 180° − 110° = 70°.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has hypotenuse 13 cm and one shorter side 5 cm. What is the other side?
Co-interior (allied) angles between parallel lines: one is 130°. What is the other?
Three angles meet at a point and are 120°, 150° and x. What is x?
questions.explain: Angles around a point sum to 360°, so x = 360° − 120° − 150° = 90°.

questions.q: Two angles in a triangle are 55° and 65°. What is the third angle?
questions.explain: Angles in a triangle sum to 180°, so 180° − 55° − 65° = 60°.

questions.q: To find a missing angle when you know the opposite and adjacent sides, which is used?
questions.explain: With opposite and adjacent you use tan, then inverse tan to get the angle.

questions.q: A triangle has base 10 cm and height 6 cm. What is its area?
A prism has cross-sectional area 12 cm^2 and length 7 cm. What is its volume?
questions.explain: Volume of a prism = cross-sectional area × length = 12 × 7 = 84 cm^3.

questions.q: A right-angled triangle has opposite = 6 and adjacent = 8. What is tan of the angle?
